questions.q: What is variation defined as in biology?
a: Differences between individuals of the same species
The process of species becoming extinct
The artificial breeding of crop plants
The duplication of chromosomes during mitosis

questions.q: Which type of variation is controlled entirely by genetic factors and results in distinct, non-overlapping categories?
What is an example of continuous variation in humans?
What causes continuous variation within a population?
a: Environmental factors alone with no genetic input
A combination of genetic control (many genes) and environmental influences

questions.q: What is a mutation defined as?
a: A genetic change in the base sequence of DNA or chromosome number, which is the source of new alleles
The normal pairing of homologous chromosomes
The division of body cells during growth
The process of natural selection acting on a population

questions.q: Which of the following factors can increase the rate of gene mutations?
a: Ionizing radiation (e.g., X-rays, UV) and chemical mutagens (e.g., tobacco tar)

questions.q: What is sickle cell anemia caused by?
a: A viral infection of red blood cells
A genetic mutation in the hemoglobin gene leading to abnormal sickle-shaped red blood cells
A bacterial toxin affecting white blood cells

questions.q: Why are individuals heterozygous for the sickle cell allele (carriers) at an advantage in malaria-endemic regions?
a: They are completely immune to all viral diseases
They run faster than normal individuals
The malaria parasite cannot reproduce successfully inside their modified red blood cells

questions.q: What is adaptive radiation or adaptation defined as?
a: The process, resulting from natural selection, by which populations become more suited to their environment over generations
The intentional choice of an animal to change its skin color
The artificial modification of genes in a laboratory setting
The physical injury of an organism during its lifetime

questions.q: What is natural selection driven by?
a: Environmental pressures, competition for resources, and differential survival and reproduction of better-adapted individuals
The deliberate choice of weak organisms to die
The uniform growth of all members of a species

questions.q: What is the key difference between natural selection and selective breeding (artificial selection)?
a: Natural selection produces identical clones; selective breeding produces variation
Natural selection is driven by humans; selective breeding is driven by nature
Natural selection is driven by environmental survival pressures; selective breeding involves humans choosing organisms with desirable traits to breed
There is no difference between them

questions.q: How do antibiotic-resistant bacteria ('superbugs') provide evidence for natural selection?
a: Antibiotics cause bacteria to mutate deliberately to survive
Bacteria can perform photosynthesis when exposed to drugs
Antibiotics have no effect on bacterial cell walls
Random mutations create resistance, and the presence of antibiotics kills non-resistant strains, leaving resistant ones to survive and reproduce

questions.q: What is the role of phenotypic variation in the process of natural selection?
a: It provides a range of characteristics so that if environmental conditions change, some individuals are more likely to possess advantageous traits and survive
It ensures that all organisms look identical
It prevents competition between different species

questions.q: Which scientist is famously known for formulating the theory of evolution by natural selection?
What happens to a population of organisms when its environment changes drastically and individuals lack suitable adaptations?
a: They immediately develop new genes to survive
They may face severe population decline or extinction
They undergo rapid mitosis to increase numbers

questions.q: Which of the following traits in humans typically shows discontinuous variation?
What is selective breeding often used for in agriculture?
a: To produce crop plants with higher yields or disease resistance, and farm animals with desirable meat or milk qualities
To eliminate all genetic variation permanently
To speed up the rotation of Earth's seasons
To turn wild animals into reptiles

questions.q: What is an adaptive feature?
a: A disease caused by a faulty gene
An inherited feature that helps an organism to survive and reproduce in its environment
A physical injury acquired during life
A temporary change in behavior due to weather

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of an adaptive feature in hydrophytes (water plants)?
a: Deep extensive root systems to find underground water
Thick waxy cuticles to prevent water loss in deserts
Large air spaces in tissues (aerenchyma) to help them float and store gases

questions.q: What is the term for a group of organisms that can reproduce to produce fertile offspring?
What causes genetic variation among offspring produced by sexual reproduction?
a: Meiosis, random assortment of chromosomes, and random fusion of gametes during fertilization
Direct copying of maternal DNA without changes

questions.q: What is the primary source of all new alleles in a population?
Which of the following best describes continuous variation data when plotted on a graph?
a: A bar chart with separate, distinct categories

questions.q: Why is genetic variation within a wild population crucial for long-term survival?
a: It allows all individuals to eat the same food
It makes organisms grow at identical rates
It prevents predators from seeing them
It ensures the population can adapt to changing environmental conditions or new diseases

questions.q: What is evolution defined as in biological science?
a: The change in adaptive features of a population over time through natural selection
The rapid physical growth of an individual organism
The division of a single cell into two clones
The static maintenance of species without alterations

questions.q: How does exposure to radiation affect DNA structure?
a: It can alter the base sequence of DNA, causing mutations
It turns DNA into protein directly
It converts animal cells into plant cells

questions.q: Which of the following characteristics in humans is influenced significantly by both genetics and environmental factors?
What is the main consequence of inbreeding in animal or plant populations?
a: An increased chance of collecting harmful recessive mutations and reduced vigor

questions.q: What type of variation is exhibited by human height?
Which of the following organisms provided classic evidence for natural selection during the Industrial Revolution due to industrial melanism?
What term describes the passing of traits from parents to offspring?
Why do xerophytes (plants adapted to dry deserts) often have reduced or needle-like leaves?
a: To catch falling rain more efficiently
To minimize surface area and reduce water loss through transpiration

questions.q: What is a mutation that occurs in body (somatic) cells rather than gametes typically unable to do?
a: Be inherited by the organism's offspring
Affect the functioning of that specific tissue
Cause abnormal cell division in that organ

questions.q: Which of the following processes ensures that chromosome numbers are halved when forming gametes?
What is the phenotypic outcome of natural selection on a well-adapted population in a stable environment?
a: Stabilizing selection preserving the existing successful features
